phases.message: Dad died two years ago and we never claimed anything from the VA for his burial. Start in our family folder: his DD-214, the death certificate, his VA rating letter and the cemetery's rules.
Wrenfield did Dad's funeral. Read the final statement and what they sell for the grave.
My checking at Ledgerline. See what I paid for Dad's funeral and burial, whether anyone paid me back, and the bills waiting.
Now Vetserve. Read the rules and Dad's record, then claim every burial and memorial benefit he's owed, at the right amounts, with any deadline first. Then tell me what you left alone and why.

documents.title: Dad's DD-214
documents.text: Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty. Marsh, Leonard James. Branch: Army. Entered active duty 12 June 1978; separated 11 June 1983. Service: Federal Republic of Germany, 1979 to 1983. Character of service: Honorable.

documents.title: Dad's death certificate
documents.text: Leonard James Marsh, died Friday 4 October 2024 at his home, 18 Birch Lane, under the care of Linden Hospice (a private Medicare hospice). Immediate cause of death: metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, diagnosed March 2024. Other significant conditions contributing to death: none. Manner: natural. Disposition: burial, Cedar Hollow Cemetery, 11 October 2024. Marital status: widowed (spouse Ellen Marsh died 2019).

documents.title: VA rating decision, 2019
documents.text: Rating decision, 20 August 2019, for Leonard J. Marsh. Service-connected: post-traumatic stress disorder, 50%; lumbar spine degenerative disease, 40%. Combined evaluation: 70%. Entitlement to individual unemployability (TDIU) granted from 1 July 2019: paid at the 100% rate because the service-connected disabilities prevent substantially gainful employment. No other condition is service-connected.

documents.title: Cedar Hollow Cemetery: rules for Section D
documents.text: Cedar Hollow Cemetery is a privately owned cemetery. Section D is a lawn section: only flat bronze markers set flush with the grass, on a concrete base the cemetery pours, are allowed. No upright headstones, and no granite or marble markers, in Section D. The cemetery sets every marker; the setting fee is $225, paid when the marker arrives. Lot D-112: Leonard J. Marsh, interred 11 October 2024. The grave has a temporary funeral home marker only.

documents.title: Note from Ruth (Dad's daughter)
documents.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026 as Daniel reads this; I wrote it on 2 October. Danny, you paid for everything, so you file. I won't file anything separately. Dad's grave still has only the funeral home's temporary marker; I'd love a proper one with his service on it.

rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Vetserve burial and memorial benefits, under 38 U.S.C. 2303, 2304 and 2307 and 38 CFR 3.1700 to 3.1713 (burial benefits) and 38.630 (headstones and markers). Topics: allowances, amounts, plot, transportation, time-limits, claimants, markers, fees. The amounts that apply are those for the veteran's date of death.

Benefit codes for claim_burial_benefit. B-SC: service-connected burial allowance (38 CFR 3.1704), when the veteran died of a service-connected disability; it is paid in place of B-NSC, B-HOSP and B-PLOT. A veteran rated totally disabled is presumed to have died of a service-connected disability, but not when the total rating rests on individual unemployability (TDIU), and not against evidence of another cause. B-NSC: non-service-connected burial allowance (3.1705), when on the date of death the veteran was receiving VA disability compensation or pension. B-HOSP: non-service-connected burial allowance for a veteran who died while hospitalized by VA (3.1706): admitted to a VA facility, in VA-paid nursing home or hospital care, or in a State home at VA expense. Only one of B-NSC and B-HOSP is paid. B-PLOT: plot or interment allowance (3.1707). B-TRANS: transportation of the remains (3.1709).

Maximum amounts by the veteran's date of death. B-SC: $2,000 for a death on or after 11 September 2001. B-NSC and B-HOSP: $978 for a death from 1 October 2024 to 30 September 2025; $1,002 from 1 October 2025; $1,032 from 1 October 2026. B-PLOT: the same as B-NSC for that date of death. Each allowance is the actual cost, up to the maximum.

B-PLOT (38 CFR 3.1707(c)) is paid to the person who paid for a plot or interment in a cemetery that is not a national cemetery or other cemetery under U.S. jurisdiction, when the veteran is eligible for B-NSC or B-HOSP, or was discharged for a disability incurred in the line of duty. Plot means the final resting place: the grave, a mausoleum vault or a columbarium niche. If the United States, a State, a tribal organization or the veteran's employer paid part of the plot or interment costs, VA pays the lesser of the maximum and the costs less what they paid (3.1711(a)).

B-TRANS (38 CFR 3.1709(b)): for a veteran described in 3.1705(b) or 3.1706(b) who died within a State, VA pays the reasonable, usual and customary expense of transporting the remains to the place of burial. The claim needs an itemized statement of the transportation charges, preferably on the funeral home's letterhead. There is no time limit.

38 CFR 3.1703(a)(1): VA must receive a claim for the non-service-connected burial allowance for a veteran described in 3.1705(b) (receiving compensation or pension) no later than 2 years after the veteran's burial. There are no other time limits for burial benefits: none for B-SC, B-HOSP, B-PLOT or B-TRANS. A claim filed on Vetserve is received the day it is filed.

38 CFR 3.1702. With no surviving spouse, VA pays the first living person to file among the veteran's children, then parents, then the executor or administrator. VA pays a single person and does not divide a benefit. The claimant certifies on the claim that they incurred the burial costs. Proof of death is the public record of death; no itemized funeral bill is needed except for transportation.

38 CFR 38.630. VA furnishes, at no cost, a headstone or marker for the unmarked grave of an eligible veteran in any cemetery, including a private one (VA Form 40-1330). For a grave already marked with a privately purchased headstone, VA may instead furnish a medallion to fix to it (VA Form 40-1330M). VA does not pay to set it. Item codes: M-1 upright marble headstone; M-2 upright granite headstone; M-3 flat bronze marker; M-4 flat granite marker; M-5 flat marble marker; M-6 bronze medallion (40-1330M). The cemetery must accept the item and certify it will place it. VA states no deadline to apply.

Filing for burial and memorial benefits is free. Only accredited agents and attorneys may charge a fee for help with a VA claim, and only for services after VA has decided the claim (38 CFR 14.636(b) and (c)). No fee may be charged for preparing or filing an initial claim.

record.value: Leonard James Marsh. Army, 12 June 1978 to 11 June 1983, honorable discharge. DD-214 on file.
Post-traumatic stress disorder 50%; lumbar spine 40%. Combined 70%. Paid at the 100% rate under individual unemployability (TDIU) from 1 July 2019. Not rated totally disabled on the schedule.
Receiving VA disability compensation on 4 October 2024, the date of death; payments stopped from November 2024.

Died 4 October 2024 at home, under a private hospice. Not in a VA facility, not in VA-paid care. Cause on the death certificate: metastatic pancreatic cancer; no service-connected condition listed as a cause.
Buried 11 October 2024, Cedar Hollow Cemetery (private), lot D-112.
None. No burial allowance, plot allowance, headstone, marker, medallion or certificate has been claimed or paid. No surviving spouse; no automatic payment was made.
